sentences.text: Puertasaurus is a genus represented by a single species, Puertasaurus reuili, which was a titanosaurian sauropod dinosaur that lived in the Late Cretaceous, approximately 70 to 68 million years ago, in what is now South America.
The fossil record consists of four vertebrae: one cervical, one dorsal, and two caudal, all found in a very fragmented state.
The largest vertebra in the holotype, believed to be the second dorsal vertebra, measures 1.06 meters high and 1.68 meters wide, making it the broadest sauropod vertebra known.
Two-thirds of the dorsal vertebra's width consists of heavily expanded transverse processes that form wing-like structures.
The preserved cervical vertebra has a transverse width of 140 centimeters, including the ribs.
It is one of the largest known dinosaurs and extends the presence of giant sauropods to the end of the Mesozoic era.
At the time, Puertasaurus was perhaps the largest sauropod in the world, distinguished by the broadest sauropod vertebra ever discovered.
The genus Puertasaurus was described by Fernando Novas and colleagues in 2005.

The holotype was discovered by Pablo Puerta and Santiago Reuil in January 2001, and the genus was named in honor of technician Pablo Puerta who made the discovery, and the species name honors Santiago Reuil who reconstructed a vertebra from about 60 fragments.
The only known specimen of Puertasaurus was found in Santa Cruz Province, southern Patagonia, Argentina.
The neural spine was oriented vertically but extremely expanded transversely, suggesting powerful neck muscles.
The vertebral centrum was especially compressed dorsoventrally with wide and deep pre- and postspinal fossae, indicating powerful neck ligaments and muscles.
Puertasaurus shared its habitat with other dinosaurs, including the large sauropod Dreadnoughtus, as well as reptiles and fish.
Puertasaurus belongs to Titanosauria, the dominant sauropod group of the Cretaceous, and is classified within the unranked family Titanosauria.

Puertasaurus is a member of the clade Lognkosauria, which includes large titanosaurs like Futalognkosaurus, Patagotitan, and Argentinosaurus, and phylogenetic analysis places Puertasaurus within the clade Lognkosauria.
Puertasaurus belongs to the parent group Colossosauria.
Puertasaurus lived during the Late Cretaceous period in southern Patagonia.
Puertasaurus lived in a humid, forested landscape during the Late Cretaceous.

Recent studies date the Cerro Fortaleza Formation, where Puertasaurus fossils were found, to between 76 and 70 million years ago, while other studies indicate the deposits belong to the Cerro Fortaleza Formation, dating to the Campanian or Maastrichtian stages, and Puertasaurus lived between 83.6 and 72.2 million years ago during the Campanian stage.
Its size is a subject of controversy because the fossil bones are enormous but very poor in both quantity and quality.

Fernando Novas estimated the species measured approximately 35 to 40 meters long and weighed between 80 and 100 metric tons, whereas Gregory S. Paul estimates a length of 30 meters and a weight of 50 tons in his reconstruction.
While generally considered a stable member of Lognkosauria, a 2017 study found Puertasaurus to be one of the least stable members of the group.
The specific formation and geological age of Puertasaurus remain debated due to inconsistent stratigraphic nomenclature in southern Patagonia.
